title: Redwood All-Hands - Sep 15 2026
summary: Leadership provided a high-level Q3 business update: strong hosted growth, Dedicated contracts progressing, Private deployments gaining traction in regulated accounts. Product demos and performance wins highlighted, SOC 2 Type II completed, focus on cost/perf optimizations. People update: selective hiring, comp review, heavier focus on engineer retention and onboarding. Roadmap emphasized reliability, routing, and cost controls. Session ended with Q&A and clear next steps for security docs, roadmap slides, and an all-hands follow-up.
action_items: Priya Singh - Share updated Q4 roadmap slide deck - 2026-09-22
Jordan Lee - Publish performance benchmark summary for Dedicated EU cluster - 2026-09-20
Samir Gupta - Send sales playbook update for enterprise Dedicated customers - 2026-09-24
Emily Zhao - Run manager sync on hiring priorities and share hiring rubric - 2026-09-21
Security Team - Upload SOC 2 Type II report and redacted controls to company drive - 2026-09-18
next_steps: Leadership to circulate slides and recording
Product to host deep-dive on Optimize recommendations next week
Security to share SOC2 assets with sales and solutions teams
People to schedule small group Q&A for compensation questions
transcript:
00:00:03 - Maya Patel: Okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, we'll kick off the all-hands, is everyone good? yes. Great. quick housekeeping, we have a 60 minute slot and we want to leave 15 minutes for questions.
00:00:23 - Maya Patel: High level agenda, Q3 recap, product highlights, security/compliance update, people org, and Q4 priorities. Jordan's going to start with a quick product note. Jordan?
00:00:35 - Jordan Lee: Thanks Maya. Quick note on runtime — we've rolled a new kernel selector that reduced tail latency for long-contexts by about 18% in our nightly tests, this is already in canary for hosted API. There's some noise in the measurements so we want more data but early signals are promising.
00:01:02 - Maya Patel: Nice. Carlos, ops/infra?
00:01:06 - Carlos Mendes: Yeah, ops update — Dedicated EU cluster is ready for initial pilot customers, we validated autoscaling, KV cache persistence across restarts, two small regressions found and fixed. We plan a soft launch next week for two customers. Memory pressure on one instance type caused small GC spikes, patched.
00:01:35 - Priya Singh: On product, Q3 we shipped streaming tool-calling improvements and structured output support for the hosted API which customer feedback shows reduced post-processing time by teams. Also Optimize launched beta and we've already given recommendations to 12 customers, with estimated savings of 15-30% on token costs.
00:02:03 - Maya Patel: Love that. Samir, commercial?
00:02:06 - Samir Gupta: Sales highlights: hosted usage up 28% QoQ, but most importantly a couple of Dedicated conversations converted to term sheets — nothing signed yet but momentum in regulated verticals. Revenue taxonomy is a bit noisy due to credits and pilot discounts, we'll clean that up in the fin ops report. Renewal rate is healthy, churn low.
00:02:33 - Maya Patel: Nice. Security update, can you lead, Priya? Or actually Security is on the line — Ben?
00:02:38 - Speaker 1 (Ben - Security): Hey everyone, quick callout — SOC 2 Type II is complete, audit period covered March through August. We have a packaged report, some redactions as normal, we'll share with customers under NDA. We also started ISO scoping, timeline looking like Q2 next year. And, SSO improvements and finer RBAC shipped.
00:03:05 - Maya Patel: Huge win, thanks Ben. Questions about compliance — will we share the report publicly?
00:03:12 - Ben: We'll share with vetted enterprise customers through the portal, not public. Also adding continuous monitoring hooks — logs to retained storage for the Dedicated customers with configurable retention.
00:03:27 - Maya Patel: Great. People update, Emily?
00:03:30 - Emily Zhao: Headcount — we're at 152, hiring is selective: we have critical roles in infra, reliability, and sales engineering. No broad freeze, but prioritization is stricter. Managers will receive updated hiring rubrics and interviewer training next week. Compensation review is underway — we will follow up with calibration sessions.
00:03:56 - Audience: mm-hmm, okay.
00:04:02 - Maya Patel: Quick finance note — burn is within plan post-Series C runway extended by disciplined hiring and better gross margins from opt-in quantized workloads. That said, we are focusing on unit economics: batching and prefix caching improvements are expected to reduce per-token cost by ~12% across the fleet.
00:04:30 - Jordan Lee: On that, the Optimize module recommendations are surfacing batching tweaks and KV cache policies per-customer; we saw a customer case where enabling prefix caching plus model quantization improved throughput 2.3x for similar latency. Not every workload can quantize, but it's working for a lot of retrieval-augmented generation patterns.
00:04:58 - Maya Patel: Ok let's drill into roadmap. Priya?
00:05:02 - Priya Singh: Q4 priorities — 1) reliability & SLOs: invest in tracing and better error classification, 2) private deployments: make the on-prem installer idempotent and reduce upgrade pain, 3) routing policies: policy engine to allow per-tenant cost vs latency tradeoffs, 4) developer experience: new SDK release. We'll schedule product deep dives for each initiative.
00:05:33 - Maya Patel: A few tactical asks — Priya, share deck after call. Jordan, can you publish the kernel selector benchmark? Carlos, confirm EU Dedicated pilot dates.
00:05:43 - Jordan Lee: Yep, will post bench notes.
00:05:45 - Carlos Mendes: Pilot customers scheduled, I'll share dates.
00:05:48 - Audience murmurs.
00:05:52 - Speaker 2 (Engineering Manager): Quick question on routing: will routing policies be per-model or per-tenant?
00:05:57 - Priya Singh: Good question. The plan is per-tenant with overrides per-route; we want tenants to pick default cost vs latency tradeoff but allow app teams to pin specific routes to low-latency variants.
00:06:12 - Speaker 3 (Sales Rep): On Dedicated pricing — any changes? Customers asked about minimum contracts.
00:06:17 - Samir Gupta: We'll finalize a new pricing tier that includes committed monthly throughput with burst credits; details going to sales next week. We are hearing requests for shorter pilots and more predictable uplift pricing.
00:06:31 - Maya Patel: I'm going to call out a couple of internal wins: product reliability up, engineering velocity improved, and great cross-functional collaboration on customer escalations. Also, marketing — the new benchmarks that Jordan and the research team produced look strong and are getting traction.
00:06:50 - Jordan Lee: Quick note on benchmarks — there's a caveat: results vary by sequence length and model family, and some names were mis-transcribed in the doc — we'll correct model identifiers and the hardware spec tables before publishing externally.
00:07:06 - Maya Patel: Okay let's open for Q&A — please use the raise hand or chat.
00:07:12 - Speaker 4 (IC): Hi — any news on international cloud partners, e.g., APAC region latency improvements?
00:07:18 - Carlos Mendes: We're onboarding a partner region for APAC later in Q4, targeting lower latency for Tokyo and Singapore regions. Capacity planning ongoing.
00:07:28 - Speaker 5 (PM): Is there a plan to expose cost recommendations directly in the console?
00:07:32 - Priya Singh: Yes, that's in the roadmap for Q4 — Optimize suggestions surfaced in Console with an explanation and expected cost delta.
00:07:40 - Speaker 6 (New Hire): I joined last month — quick ask on onboarding docs and getting access to sandboxes?
00:07:44 - Emily Zhao: We'll run a new hire cohort next Thursday, there will be hands-on sandboxes and buddy assignments, reach out to people ops for access.
00:07:53 - Speaker 7 (Sales Engineer): Regarding SOC2 assets, will we have a standard NDA path? Our reps need a link to share.
00:07:59 - Ben - Security: Yes, we'll add a gated portal link and a one-click NDA for redaction-heavy materials, pushing to sales later this week.
00:08:08 - Maya Patel: Anything else? Okay, I want to give a couple of context on metrics — monthly active developers using our API up 33% this quarter, net new signups driven by PLG templates and onboarding flow improvements. We still have some churn in a small vertical — we'll follow-up.
00:08:29 - Jordan Lee: Also dev experience — SDK v2 includes better streaming hooks and reduced reconnect churn for flaky networks.
00:08:38 - Maya Patel: Alright closing notes: Thank you teams for strong quarter execution. For the next week: product deep-dive schedule, security folder share, and hiring rubric distribution. We'll reconvene next all-hands in one month.
00:08:56 - Maya Patel: Quick lightning round — shoutouts?
00:09:01 - Several participants: shoutouts to infra and security teams.
00:09:10 - Maya Patel: Great, meeting wrap. Recording and slides will be circulated.
00:09:15 - End of recording.
